expected.charges: Freedom Ride participation — rode through Montgomery to Jackson, arrested May 28, 1961.
expected.convicted: Convicted; judgment reversed by the U.S. Supreme Court on April 26, 1965 (Thomas v. Mississippi, 380 U.S. 524).
expected.sentence: Municipal court imposed a suspended 60-day sentence and a $200 fine; the county-court retrial imposed four months and a $200 fine. These are sentences, not verified time served. The U.S. Supreme Court reversed the conviction on April 26, 1965. Individual custody endpoints remain separately documented or unresolved.

updates.sentence: Municipal court imposed a suspended 60-day sentence and a $200 fine; the county-court retrial imposed four months and a $200 fine. These are sentences, not verified time served. The U.S. Supreme Court reversed the conviction on April 26, 1965. Individual custody endpoints remain separately documented or unresolved. Michael Booth’s interview-based account reports 41 days actually confined, including Hinds County Jail and Parchman. The individual release day remains unverified; no endpoint is calculated from this total. Source: https://www.crmvet.org/mem/ofosu.htm
